newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PX50 EDGES HIGHER, BLUE CHIPS MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PX50 EDGES HIGHER, BLUE CHIPS MIXED.

text.p: Czech shares edged slightly higher at Monday's fixing on the Prague bourse despite mixed performances from the PX50 index's most highly capitalised issues.
Two of the four biggest high caps, CEZ and Ceska Sporitelna were unchanged on 910 and 275 respectively while SPT Telecom edged up 13 crowns to 3,638 and Komercni Banka lost five crowns to 1,635.
The four above issues account for 49.5 percent of PX50 index capitalisation and are generally the most heavily traded shares by foreign investors.
Dealers said that nervousness among foreign investors following heavy flooding in the Czech Republic would continue to dent confidence in the equity market.

"If foreigners have any holdings..they are now very much worried by their involvement in particular companies," said Lubomir Vystavel referring specifically to potential problems for banks beacuse of bad debts.
Construction companies, however, would benefit in the longer term. At Monday's fixing the biggest building stocks were all down. Metrostav dropped 21 crowns to 2,229.
